speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; have you noticed any abdominal distension or pain since birth?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given your brother's history of pyloric stenosis, are there any signs of a high obstruction, such as non-bilious projectile vomiting, or is the vomit definitely green/bilious? Have you noticed any blood in the stool or signs of dehydration like decreased wet diapers?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Bilious vomiting. I also have Feeding intolerance, No fever, Vomiting started within first day after birth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal Ultrasound. REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_X-Ray. Please tell me if there is any abdominal distension or if you have noticed any "currant jelly" stools.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Atresia
